title: Drawing people
examples: How do I make a person look like they are moving?
What is the best way to draw a hand?
Should I draw the whole body or just the head?

explain.say: Today we will learn how to draw people using simple rules.

items: Add simple shapes for body parts.

explain.say: First we look at proportions, which are the relative sizes of body parts.
A simple rule is that the whole person is often about seven to eight heads tall.
Next we look at gesture drawing, which captures the movement or action.
For a real-life example, look at a running person in the park.
A common mistake is drawing every part perfectly straight and rigid.

faq.q: How do I know if my proportions are correct?
faq.a: You can compare the drawing to a known reference or use the head measurement guide. You might also ask, 'Does this person look too tall or too short?' or 'How many heads is this person?'
asks: What is the head measurement rule?
How do I check my drawing size?

faq.q: What is the difference between proportion and gesture?
faq.a: Proportion is about the correct size relationship between body parts. Gesture drawing is about capturing the energy and movement in the pose. You could also ask, 'Should I worry about size or movement first?' or 'What do I focus on when drawing action?'
asks: What is the main goal of gesture drawing?

faq.q: Do I need to draw the whole body every time?
faq.a: No, you can focus on just the head or just the action. It is fine to draw only parts if that is what the pose shows. You might ask, 'Can I skip drawing the feet?' or 'What if I only have a picture of a face?'
asks: Can I draw just the upper body?
What if I only see a quick snapshot?

faq.q: Is there a standard measurement for everything?
faq.a: While the head measurement is a good guide, remember that people vary greatly in size. Use it as a starting point, not a strict rule. You could ask, 'Are there exceptions to the head rule?' or 'Can I draw a giant person?'
asks: Does art history change these rules?
Is this rule for all people?

faq.q: What drawing materials are best for gesture drawing?
faq.a: Light materials like charcoal or a light pencil are best because you want to make mistakes. You should draw loosely and quickly. You might ask, 'Should I use black ink?' or 'What is the best pencil grade?'
asks: What is the easiest medium to practice with?

facts: The head is often used as a unit of measurement for the whole body.
Gesture drawing focuses on the line of action and energy of a pose.
Human proportions are generally consistent across many cultures.
Drawing in stages helps you build accuracy from simple shapes.

quiz.say: If a person is drawn to be exactly seven and a half heads tall, what is the best approach?

options.show: The body should show clear signs of movement or curve.
options.say: The body should show clear signs of movement or curve.

options.show: The drawing must be perfectly straight and vertical.
options.say: The drawing must be perfectly straight and vertical.

options.show: The height must be exactly seven heads.
options.say: The height must be exactly seven heads.

options.show: Only the head size matters for the whole figure.
options.say: Only the head size matters for the whole figure.

quiz.why: The correct answer focuses on gesture, which captures movement, even if the proportions are slightly adjusted.

wrong.1: This is tempting because it seems neat, but it ignores the natural curves of the body.
wrong.2: This is tempting because it uses a whole number, but people are rarely perfect whole numbers.
wrong.3: This is tempting because the head is a key unit, but it ignores the size of the torso and limbs.

quiz.say: When drawing a figure in motion, what should be the first thing you focus on?

options.show: The main curved line showing the pose's energy.
options.say: The main curved line showing the pose's energy.

options.show: Drawing the head first to set the scale.
options.say: Drawing the head first to set the scale.

options.show: Drawing the feet to make the figure grounded.
options.say: Drawing the feet to make the figure grounded.

quiz.why: Gesture drawing starts with the line of action, which is the core curve that defines the pose's energy.

wrong.0: This is tempting because it seeks accuracy, but it slows down the capture of quick energy.
wrong.2: This is tempting because the head is a key unit, but it locks you into a static view.
wrong.3: This is tempting because it feels stable, but it misses the overall flow of the movement.

quiz.say: If you are using the head as a measure, and you draw a person that is clearly leaning, what should you do?

options.show: Use curves to show the weight shift across the body.
options.say: Use curves to show the weight shift across the body.

options.show: Draw the figure as if standing perfectly upright.
options.say: Draw the figure as if standing perfectly upright.

options.show: Ignore the lean and just draw the head size.
options.say: Ignore the lean and just draw the head size.

options.show: Use only straight lines for the structure.
options.say: Use only straight lines for the structure.

quiz.why: When leaning, the body's weight creates natural curves, which is what gesture drawing captures best.

wrong.1: This is tempting because it is the default, but it ignores the actual dynamic pose shown.
wrong.2: This is tempting because it is simple, but it loses the entire sense of balance and action.
wrong.3: This is tempting because it is easy to draw, but it makes the figure look stiff and unnatural.
